name: Google AI Studio / Gemini API
tagline: The only free tier that hands you a 1M-token context window, but Google quietly moved every Pro model behind billing in April 2026 — treat Flash as the free tier and plan around it.
quota: Permanent rate-limited free tier, no credits. Flash / Flash-Lite family plus Gemma 4 models. Per-model daily request budgets in the hundreds-to-1,500 range. Pro-tier models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 3 Pro, 3.1 Pro) were removed from the free tier on 2026-04-01 and now require billing.
limits: unknown
region_notes: Available in most regions. Outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, free-tier prompts and responses may be reviewed/used to improve Google products. Some features (Grounding, Search) are not available on the free tier.
best_for: Long-document RAG without a vector DB
Multimodal prototypes (image, audio, PDF, video)
Hobby projects that need a big context window for free
quickstart:
Sign in at aistudio.google.com with a Google account, click 'Get API key' in the left nav, and create the key in a new or existing Cloud project. Do NOT enable billing on that project — doing so reportedly cancels the free allowance for the whole project, so keep paid and experimental keys in separate projects. Check your real per-model numbers in the AI Studio rate-limit dashboard.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gemini-3.6-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this in one sentence: free tiers change fast."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: high on existence of the free tier and on no-card signup; LOW on exact per-model numbers. The official rate-limits page (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits) was unreachable during this research (fetch failed repeatedly), and Google no longer publishes a static table — it points you at your AI Studio dashboard. Multiple independent secondary sources (Aug 2026) agree on roughly 10-15 RPM and up to ~1,500 RPD for the Flash family, and 5 RPM / 50-100 RPD where 2.5 Pro is still reachable, but these are NOT official figures. Verify in your own dashboard before publishing exact numbers.

name: Groq Cloud
tagline: Still the fastest free inference on the planet, and the model lineup rotates constantly — check the limits page before you hard-code a model ID, because last quarter's workhorse may be gone.
quota: Permanent free plan, rate-limited per model (no credit balance on the free plan). Includes text models, prompt-guard classifiers, and Whisper speech-to-text. Limits are per organization, not per user.
limits: Free plan, from the official Groq rate-limits page: openai/gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b: 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 8K TPM / 200K TPD. qwen/qwen3.6-27b: 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 8K TPM / 200K TPD. qwen/qwen3.8-27b: 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 8K TPM / 2M TPD. groq/compound and groq/compound-mini: 30 RPM / 250 RPD / 70K TPM. meta-llama/llama-prompt-guard-2-22m and -86m: 30 RPM / 14,400 RPD / 15K TPM / 500K TPD. whisper-large-v3 and whisper-large-v3-turbo: 20 RPM / 2,000 RPD / 7.2K audio-seconds per hour / 28.8K per day. canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english and orpheus-arabic-saudi: 10 RPM / 100 RPD / 1.2K TPM / 3.6K TPD. Cached tokens do not count toward limits.
region_notes: US data centers. No credit card or phone verification reported for the free plan.
best_for: Voice agents and anything where time-to-first-token matters
Streaming chat UIs that need to feel instant
Free Whisper transcription at meaningful volume
quickstart:
Register at console.groq.com with an email, then go to API Keys and create a key. No card is needed on the Free plan. Open the Limits page in account settings to see the exact caps for your org, since model availability rotates.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_GROQ_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain LPU inference in two sentences."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Limits table read directly from the official Groq docs page (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits) during this research. Note the free-plan model list is short and changes often — Llama 3.3 70B and Llama 4 Scout appear in older write-ups but were not in the current free-plan table.

name: Cerebras Inference
tagline: Used to be the most generous no-card free tier in this list. As of August 2026 it is a $5 card-gated trial that dies in 30 days — include it, but do not build on it.
quota: $5 in free credits. Every model on the public Model Catalog is usable on the trial, subject to per-model trial rate limits.
limits: Free Trial per model: gpt-oss-120b — 5 RPM / 30K TPM / 1M tokens per hour / 1M tokens per day. gemma-4-31b — 5 RPM / 30K TPM / 1M TPH / 1M TPD, with image input capped at 2 per request and 4 MB payload. Any metric can trigger a 429, whichever is hit first.
region_notes: No region restriction reported. A verified payment method is mandatory — Playground and API access stay inactive until you add one.
best_for: Benchmarking wafer-scale inference speed before committing budget
A short burst of high-throughput token generation
quickstart:
Create an account at cloud.cerebras.ai, add a verified payment method (required — nothing is charged until you buy more), and generate an API key. Your $5 appears on the account and expires 30 days after it is granted.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_CEREBRAS_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.cerebras.ai/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why is wafer-scale inference fast?"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH, and this is the biggest correction in the dataset. Read directly from the official Cerebras rate-limits docs, which state plainly: 'Cerebras doesn't currently offer a no-cost tier that renews automatically or a per-model always-free allowance.' Many comparison articles still list Cerebras as '1M tokens/day, no card' — that is stale. Models listed in Choose-a-Model beyond the public catalog are Dedicated-Endpoints only.

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tagline: Neurons are a deliberately opaque billing unit, which is the point — you get a real daily allowance at the edge, but you will not know how far it goes until you run something.
quota: 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge, on both Free and Paid Workers plans. Paid users keep the same 10,000/day free allocation and are billed $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons above it. Covers 50+ models: text generation, embeddings, image generation, Whisper-class ASR, TTS, reranking, translation.
limits: 10,000 Neurons per day, account-wide, resetting daily at 00:00 UTC. Exceeding any limit returns an error until reset. Conversion examples from the official pricing table: gpt-oss-120b is 31,818 Neurons per M input / 68,182 per M output; gemma-4-26b-a4b-it is 9,091 / 27,273; bge-m3 embeddings are 1,075 Neurons per M input tokens; Whisper is 41.14 Neurons per audio minute.
region_notes: Runs on Cloudflare's global edge network. No card needed for the free allowance. Note: a handful of frontier models (@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, deepseek-v4-pro-0813) require a paid Workers plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits.
best_for: Serverless inference colocated with your app on the edge
Cheap embeddings and reranking in a RAG pipeline
Set-and-forget free daily budget for low-traffic side projects
quickstart:
Create a free Cloudflare account at dash.cloudflare.com, go to AI > Workers AI, and grab your Account ID plus an API token. Call the REST endpoint with your account ID; no card is required for the 10,000 Neuron daily allowance.

```python
# pip install requests
import requests, os

ACCOUNT_ID = os.environ["CF_ACCOUNT_ID"]
TOKEN = os.environ["CF_API_TOKEN"]

r = requests.post(
    f"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/run/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"},
    json={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is a Neuron?"}]},
)
print(r.json()["result"]["response"])
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Read from the official Cloudflare Workers AI pricing page, last updated 2026-08-28 — the day before this research. Not OpenAI-compatible by default (Cloudflare-specific REST shape), though an OpenAI-compatible binding exists.

name: OpenRouter (:free models)
tagline: The widest free model catalog behind one key, with the honest caveat that free endpoints can vanish overnight — never hard-code a :free model in a production path.
quota: Free model variants (IDs ending in :free) are usable with no card. Requests are capped per day, not by a token or dollar balance.
limits: From the official OpenRouter limits doc: with under 10 credits purchased (all time) — 20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day. With at least 10 credits purchased — 20 requests/minute and 1,000 requests/day. The cap is global across accounts and keys; making more accounts or keys does not raise it. Cloudflare DDoS protection applies on top.
region_notes: No region restriction reported. Requests route through OpenRouter's infrastructure before reaching the upstream provider.
best_for: A/B testing a prompt across many model families
One key as a fallback behind your primary provider
Comparing DeepSeek vs Llama vs Qwen without five signups
quickstart:
Sign up at openrouter.ai, create a key, and browse openrouter.ai/models filtered to free models. Anything ending in :free costs nothing; a one-time $10 top-up raises your daily cap from 50 to 1,000. Add HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers to see per-project usage.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_OPENROUTER_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openrouter/free",  # auto-picks from available free models
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
    extra_headers={"HTTP-Referer": "https://yoursite.dev", "X-Title": "my-app"},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the limits numbers (read from openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits). The free model pool itself changes constantly — secondary sources cited anywhere from 16 to 30 free models across 2026, and specific families (DeepSeek free variants, Llama, Qwen3 endpoints) were reported delisted at various points. Do not publish a fixed model count.

name: NVIDIA NIM / build.nvidia.com
tagline: Credits that reportedly never expire across a 100+ model catalog — the catch is that 'credits' are not tokens, and nobody publishes how fast a big model eats them.
quota: 1,000 free inference credits on signup, reportedly expandable to 5,000 on request. Credits reportedly do not expire. Covers LLMs, vision, image generation, speech, and simulation models.
limits: 40 requests per minute (secondary sources; not confirmed on an official page). Larger models consume more credits per request — each model page lists its credit cost.
region_notes: Phone verification is reported as required after email verification. No region restriction reported.
best_for: Sampling a very wide model catalog on one key
Testing frontier open-weight MoEs (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM) before paying
Vision, speech and 3D/simulation models that narrow providers do not carry
quickstart:
Register a free NVIDIA Developer account at build.nvidia.com, verify email (and phone, if prompted), then generate an API key from account settings — the key starts with nvapi- and is shown only once. Credits are applied automatically; use 'Request More' if you need the higher allocation.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1",
    api_key="nvapi-YOUR_KEY",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain GPU compute in one paragraph."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. The 1,000-credits / 5,000-on-request / no-expiry / no-card / 40-RPM figures come from multiple independent secondary sources that agree with each other, but I could not confirm them on an official NVIDIA page — the build.nvidia.com homepage says only 'Free inference with leading models' and docs.nvidia.com/NIM covers self-hosted containers, not the hosted free tier. Treat the numbers as unverified and re-check before publishing.

name: Cohere (Trial key)
tagline: Ignore the chat models — the reason to hold a Cohere trial key is Embed and Rerank, which are unusually generous on the free tier and genuinely best-in-class for RAG.
quota: Free evaluation ('trial') key. Chat is capped at 1,000 API calls per month across trial keys and newer model variants. Embed and Rerank have per-minute limits rather than a monthly cap.
limits: From the official Cohere rate-limits page. Trial: Chat models (Command A, Command A+, Command R, Command R+, Command R7B, Command A Vision, Command A Translate, Command A Reasoning, North Mini Code) — 20 req/min, 1,000 calls/month. Rerank — 10 req/min. Embed — 2,000 inputs/min. Embed (images) — 5 inputs/min. EmbedJob — 5 req/min. Tokenize — 100 req/min. Audio Transcriptions — 5 req/min. Parse — 500 req/min.
region_notes: No region restriction reported. Trial keys are non-commercial.
best_for: RAG pipelines that need real Embed + Rerank quality
Multilingual retrieval (Aya family)
Prototyping a reranker before paying a per-search tax
quickstart:
Create an account at dashboard.cohere.com, then open API Keys and generate a trial key — no card is required for the trial tier. Install the SDK and call Embed or Rerank; chat is limited to 1,000 calls per month.

```python
# pip install cohere
import cohere

co = cohere.ClientV2("YOUR_TRIAL_KEY")

resp = co.rerank(
    model="rerank-v3.5",
    query="Which provider has the best free GPU tier?",
    documents=["Kaggle gives 30 GPU hours a week", "Modal gives $30 a month", "Colab is dynamic"],
    top_n=2,
)
for r in resp.results:
    print(r.index, r.relevance_score)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on limits (read directly from docs.cohere.com/docs/rate-limits). card_required=false is MEDIUM confidence — the official page does not state card policy; multiple secondary sources say no card is needed for a trial key. One secondary source claims trial keys expire after ~3 months; the official page does not mention expiry, so expiry is recorded as no-expiry.

name: Mistral La Plateforme (Experiment)
tagline: Roughly a billion tokens a month on every model including the flagship, which sounds unbeatable until you read the terms: your API traffic becomes their training data.
quota: Free 'Experiment' plan covering all models — Mistral Large, Small, Codestral, Pixtral, embeddings, OCR. Approximately 1 billion tokens per month.
limits: Reported as ~1-2 requests per second, 500,000 tokens per minute, ~1 billion tokens per month. Phone verification required; no credit card.
region_notes: EU data residency — the only genuinely free tier in this dataset processed on European infrastructure. Phone (SMS) verification is mandatory, with no way around it.
best_for: GDPR-sensitive prototyping that must stay on EU infrastructure
Code generation with Codestral at volume
European-language workloads where Mistral outperforms
quickstart:
Sign up at console.mistral.ai, verify your phone number by SMS, select the free 'Experiment' plan, and create a key under API Keys. If data privacy matters, look for the opt-out in settings before you send anything proprietary.

```python
# pip install mistralai
import os
from mistralai import Mistral

client = Mistral(api_key=os.environ["MISTRAL_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.complete(
    model="mistral-large-latest",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Compare Rust and Python for ML inference."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. Several independent secondary sources converge on ~1 RPS / 500K TPM / 1B tokens per month / phone verification / no card / data used for training, but docs.mistral.ai and help.mistral.ai both failed to load during this research, so no figure here is from an official page. The data-training flag is the one to get right — every source that mentions it agrees free-tier traffic may be used for model improvement.

name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
tagline: Unmatched model breadth at pass-through pricing, but the free account's monthly credit is close to a rounding error — this is a discovery surface, not a free tier to build on.
quota: unknown
limits: Free accounts: 1,000 API requests per 5-minute window and 5,000 resolver requests per 5-minute window (from the official Hub plan comparison). No published free model-token allowance.
region_notes: No region restriction reported.
best_for: Trying an obscure open-weight model you cannot host elsewhere
Quick sanity checks across the Hub's 200+ served models
Developers already paying for PRO who want pooled inference credits
quickstart:
Create a free account at huggingface.co, generate a read access token under Settings > Access Tokens, and call the router endpoint. Add a payment method if you need anything beyond the small free allowance — Inference Providers are pay-as-you-go for free accounts.

```python
# pip install huggingface_hub
from huggingface_hub import InferenceClient

client = InferenceClient(token="hf_YOUR_TOKEN")

out = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "One sentence on why credits matter."}],
)
print(out.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE on rate limits: HIGH (read from the official Hub Team/Enterprise plan doc, which lists Free as 1,000 API requests and 5,000 resolver requests per 5-minute window). CONFIDENCE on free credits: LOW. The same official doc lists Inference Providers for Free accounts as 'PAYG' with no included credit, while several secondary sources cite '$0.10/month' for free and '$2/month' for PRO. Because official and secondary disagree, quota and expiry are recorded as unknown rather than picking a number. Do not publish $0.10 as fact.

name: xAI Grok API
tagline: The biggest dollar amounts in this dataset, and the most expensive fine print: the recurring $150/month requires permanently switching on training-data sharing, and you cannot switch it back off.
quota: $25 in one-time promotional credits on signup. Separately, an ongoing $150/month in free credits is available if you enable data sharing, reportedly after spending at least $5 first — taking the first month to roughly $175.
limits: unknown
region_notes: No region restriction reported. A card is required to open a console.x.ai account.
best_for: Solo developers and OSS maintainers with no confidentiality constraints
Benchmarking a 2M-context model on throwaway code
Hackathon teams who can afford to have their prompts ingested
quickstart:
Register at console.x.ai with a card on file, then create a key under API Keys. The $25 promotional credit appears in Billing. If you want the recurring $150, enable data sharing under Settings > Data Sharing — read the terms first, because multiple sources describe the switch as irreversible for the team.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="xai-YOUR_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="grok-4-fast",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize my repo's architecture."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: LOW-MEDIUM and this entry should be flagged on the site. docs.x.ai failed to load during this research, so every figure comes from secondary sources that describe the program differently: some say $25/month resetting monthly, others say $25 one-time expiring in 30 days, and the $150/month data-sharing grant is described as requiring prior spend and a permanent, team-level opt-in. I recorded the more conservative reading (one-time $25, 30 days) and noted the discrepancy. Verify before publishing.

name: Vercel AI Gateway
tagline: Five dollars a month of someone else's frontier models at provider list price with zero markup — the smallest recurring free credit here, but the only one that reaches GPT and Claude-class models.
quota: $5 per month in AI Gateway Credits, applied automatically on your first request. Only 'Free Tier eligible' models in the catalog can be charged against free credits. Once you purchase credits your team moves to the paid tier and the monthly free credit no longer applies.
limits: Free tier requests are rate limited per model, with lower limits than the paid tier. Exceeding a limit returns a 429. Vercel does not publish exact free-tier numbers per model.
region_notes: Requires a Vercel team account. BYOK is not available on the free tier. Zero Data Retention and team-wide provider allowlists are Pro/Enterprise features.
best_for: Trying frontier proprietary models without a per-provider signup
Teams already on Vercel who want one endpoint and one invoice
Prototyping against GPT/Claude-class models on a small budget
quickstart:
Create a Vercel account, open the AI Gateway tab in your dashboard, and generate a gateway API key. Browse vercel.com/ai-gateway/models?freeTier=true to see which models the free credits cover — your $5 starts on your first request and refreshes monthly.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_AI_GATEWAY_KEY",
    base_url="https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.6-luna",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about rate limits."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Read directly from the official Vercel AI Gateway pricing page. Note the important asymmetry the docs state: purchasing credits permanently moves the team off the monthly free credit. The subset of free-tier-eligible models is not enumerated on the pricing page, so 'which models' is a dashboard lookup.

name: Fireworks AI
tagline: One dollar. That is the whole free tier — enough to prove the SDK works, not enough to evaluate anything, which tells you exactly who Fireworks is optimizing for.
quota: $1 in one-time credits for new accounts. Afterwards it is standard postpaid per-token billing.
limits: Reported as 10 requests/minute with no card on file, rising to 6,000 RPM with a card. Monthly spend tiers gate at $50 / $500 / $5,000 / $50,000.
region_notes: No region restriction reported. Fireworks publishes a default zero-data-retention policy for open models.
best_for: Verifying an OpenAI-compatible integration end to end
Function calling and structured output smoke tests
Latency benchmarking against a FireAttention stack
quickstart:
Sign up at fireworks.ai and grab your key from the dashboard — new accounts get $1 in credit, no card required. Add a card only if you need to clear the no-card RPM ceiling.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1",
    api_key="YOUR_FIREWORKS_KEY",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. The $1 credit is consistently reported across several 2026 reviews and is corroborated by a pricing comparison that cites Fireworks' own billing docs. The 10 RPM no-card figure comes from one secondary source. Fireworks also runs a promo-code 'Fire Pass' giving zero per-token pricing on one rotating open-weight model, but it is restricted to personal use in agentic coding harnesses and prohibited for production — deliberately not counted as a free tier here.

name: DeepSeek Platform
tagline: Five million tokens for thirty days with no card is the most usable evaluation budget on this list — just be clear-eyed that your prompts land on servers in China.
quota: 5 million free tokens for new developer accounts, valid 30 days. Worth roughly $8 at V4-Flash rates. Covers both model IDs the platform now ships (deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro).
limits: Reported as 2,500 concurrent requests on V4-Flash and 500 on V4-Pro. No published per-minute request cap confirmed.
region_notes: The official api.deepseek.com endpoint is reachable from US and EU IPs and accepts international cards. All personal data processed through the official API is stored on servers in China, and DeepSeek's privacy policy grants broad data rights — a hard blocker for regulated, HIPAA or defence-adjacent workloads. US federal and several state agencies ban DeepSeek on government-furnished equipment.
best_for: Cheapest frontier-adjacent reasoning for a 30-day evaluation
Long-context workloads that need a full 1M-token window
Teams comfortable with China-hosted inference
quickstart:
Create an account at platform.deepseek.com, verify your email, and generate a key under API Keys — the 5M token grant appears immediately and expires in 30 days whether you use it or not. Plan to run your eval matrix in weeks one and two, not week four.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-YOUR_DEEPSEEK_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.deepseek.com",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-v4-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this function for clarity."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH. The 5M tokens / 30 days / no card figure is consistent across several independent 2026 sources including two pricing trackers. Concurrency figures are secondary. Important: the older deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner IDs were retired 2026-07-24; configs still using them will fail. Data-residency concerns are well documented and should be surfaced on the site.

name: Z.ai (GLM, Zhipu international)
tagline: A genuinely permanent free tier with a 200K context window and no card — throttled to a single concurrent request, which makes it a solo-developer tool and nothing else.
quota: $0 input and $0 output, permanently, on GLM-4.7-Flash (~200K context, tuned for coding and agents), GLM-4.5-Flash (128K), and GLM-4.6V-Flash (vision). Paid models start at GLM-4.7-FlashX ($0.07/$0.40) which lifts the concurrency cap.
limits: 1 concurrent request, roughly 1 request per second on the free models. GLM-4.7-Flash maxes out at 16,384 output tokens.
region_notes: The international endpoint is api.z.ai (Z.ai), distinct from the China-based open.bigmodel.cn which requires a Chinese phone number. Register via email, Google or GitHub on z.ai. Latency outside Asia may be noticeable.
best_for: Solo coding agents and sequential batch jobs
The only free vision-language model worth wiring up
Long-context coding on a permanent (not trial) budget
quickstart:
Register at z.ai (email, Google or GitHub — no card), open the API Keys page and generate a key. The endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so the standard openai library works with only base_url and model changed. Use glm-4.7-flash for free coding work and switch to glm-4.7-flashx if you need concurrency.

```python
# pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_ZAI_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="glm-4.7-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reverse a linked list in Python."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. The three permanently free models, $0 pricing and 1-concurrency limit are reported consistently by several 2026 sources and corroborated by Z.ai's own pricing docs as cited by them. I confirmed the OpenAI-compatible base URL and current model naming directly from docs.z.ai, but that quick-start page does not mention the free tier. name: Google Colab
tagline: The default answer everyone gives, and in 2026 it is the weakest of the three big notebook tiers — no published quota, no GPU guarantee, and idle-kills that punish long runs.
quota: No published fixed allowance. Free-tier GPU access is dynamic and demand-driven; Google explicitly does not promise a GPU or a particular GPU model. Typically an NVIDIA T4 (16 GB), sometimes downgraded to older hardware under load.
limits: Notebook VMs run for at most 12 hours and can end much sooner. Idle sessions disconnect aggressively (commonly reported at 30-90 minutes). Session limits, idle timeouts and available hardware all fluctuate with demand and your recent usage. Secondary estimates put the practical weekly allowance around 15-30 GPU hours; Google does not publish this.
region_notes: No card needed. Roughly 12.7 GB system RAM, ephemeral disk. Paid plans (Pro £9.72/mo, Pro+ £45.90/mo) allocate compute units rather than removing limits, and exhausting them drops you back to free-tier policy.
best_for: Teaching and demos, where the familiar UX matters
Quick experiments under an hour
Getting a GPU with zero setup as a first step
quickstart:
Go to colab.research.google.com, open a notebook, and select Runtime > Change runtime type > T4 GPU. Always print the device name first — if you were handed weaker hardware, factory-reset the runtime and retry later. Mount Google Drive for anything you need to keep.

```python
import torch
print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
print(round(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9, 1), "GB")

# Always checkpoint — a free session can die at any moment.
import os
CKPT = "/content/drive/MyDrive/ckpt.pt"
if os.path.exists(CKPT):
    print("resuming from checkpoint")
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM on the qualitative picture (no published quota, dynamic allocation, 12h cap) — this is consistent across official position summaries and multiple independent 2026 tests. The 15-30 GPU-hours-per-week number is explicitly an estimate from secondary sources, NOT an official figure; quota reflects this honestly. The official Colab FAQ page failed to load during this research.

name: Kaggle Notebooks
tagline: Thirty GPU hours a week on a counter you can actually read — in 2026 this is the most reliable free GPU on the internet, and almost nobody recommends it.
quota: Weekly GPU quota of 30 hours, sometimes higher depending on demand and resources, resetting weekly. One NVIDIA Tesla P100 (16 GB) or a T4 x2 configuration (32 GB combined), plus free TPU v3-8. CPU usage is unlimited.
limits: 12 hours maximum execution for CPU and GPU sessions, 9 hours for TPU. 'Save & Run All' must also complete within that window. 20 minutes of idle time on an interactive session (60 minutes for batch sessions). 29 GB RAM on P100 and T4 x2 configs, 20 GB autosave disk. Internet is enabled by default. Availability is limited and you may queue at busy times.
region_notes: No card needed, but phone verification is required to unlock GPU and TPU accelerators. Notebooks on the free tier are public by default, so do not put sensitive data in them. Colab Pro subscribers can link their account for an extra 15 GPU hours/week (30 for Pro+).
best_for: LoRA and QLoRA fine-tuning of models up to ~7B
Long training runs that need a predictable quota counter
Anything involving Kaggle's hosted datasets, which mount fast
quickstart:
Create a Kaggle account and verify your phone number — without it the Accelerator menu stays locked. Open a new Notebook, go to Settings > Accelerator and pick GPU P100 or TPU v3-8. Enable Persistence (Files only) so checkpoints survive a session restart.

```python
import torch
print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))

# P100 has no bf16 tensor cores — fp16 with a GradScaler is the safe path.
from torch.cuda.amp import GradScaler, autocast
scaler = GradScaler()
with autocast(dtype=torch.float16):
    out = torch.nn.Linear(1024, 1024).cuda()(torch.randn(8, 1024).cuda())
print(out.shape)
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. The 30-hours-per-week quota is confirmed on Kaggle's own docs page (kaggle.com/docs/efficient-gpu-usage: 'The quota resets weekly and is 30 hours or sometimes higher depending on demand and resources'). Session limits, hardware specs, RAM, disk and TPU availability all read from kaggle.com/docs/notebooks. Phone verification is confirmed by community answers on kaggle.com rather than the docs page. P100 is the only GPU the docs explicitly describe as free to add; T4 x2 appears in the technical spec table.

name: Hugging Face Spaces (ZeroGPU)
tagline: Five minutes a day on a Blackwell is not a training tier — it is the cheapest way in existence to put a GPU-backed demo behind a public URL and let strangers use it.
quota: 5 minutes of ZeroGPU time per day on a free account. 2 minutes per day unauthenticated, 40 minutes on PRO ($9/mo), 60 minutes on Team and Enterprise. Time-slices NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell accelerators (48 GB default, 96 GB on the xlarge tier at 2x quota cost).
limits: 5 min/day included quota, pooled across your Spaces. Roughly 60 seconds maximum per @spaces.GPU decorated call on the free tier. A free personal account in good standing can host 2 Gradio Spaces on ZeroGPU plus unlimited Static Spaces. Spaces sleep after 48 hours idle, with a ~30-90s cold start. Outbound network restricted to ports 80, 443 and 8080.
region_notes: No card needed and no non-commercial clause — commercial use is allowed, though the free tier carries no uptime guarantee. Region is not user-selectable. Free Spaces serve from *.hf.space only; custom domains need PRO or above. Visitors consume their own quota, not yours.
best_for: Publishing a model demo that real people can click
Portfolio pieces and hackathon submissions with a live URL
Short burst inference where idle cost must be zero
quickstart:
Create a free HF account, verify your email and wait out the 30-day account-age requirement for 'good standing', then create a Gradio Space with ZeroGPU hardware. Decorate only your inference function — the GPU attaches during the call and detaches immediately after, so idle costs nothing.

```python
# app.py
import gradio as gr
import spaces

@spaces.GPU(duration=60)  # free tier: keep calls short
def generate(prompt):
    return f"running on GPU: {prompt}"

gr.Interface(fn=generate, inputs="text", outputs="text").launch()
```
notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the quota ladder (2 / 5 / 40 minutes, $1 per 10 minutes beyond) — read from Hugging Face's own docs. Note the important 2026 change several sources report: Gradio and Docker Spaces now require a paid plan to create, with a carve-out letting free accounts in good standing host up to 2 ZeroGPU Gradio Spaces. Static Spaces remain free for everyone. ZeroGPU is Gradio-SDK only, PyTorch 2.8+, Python 3.10 or 3.12.

name: Modal

limits: Starter plan: 3 workspace seats, 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency, 200 deployed apps, 5 cron jobs, 1-day log retention. region_notes: Includes 1 TiB/month of free volume storage. SOC 2 compliant. Region selection is available on the free plan at a premium multiplier.
best_for: Serverless GPU functions that scale to zero between calls
